hero.eyebrow: MIT licensed · React Native and Expo
hero.title: Foundation libraries for
hero.lead: Small, focused, dependency-light packages. Drop one in and carry on — there is no framework here to adopt.

packages.title: What is published
packages.body: Each package is released and documented on its own. Two are out today; the rest are still being written, and get a page here when they are real.

items.name: @axonpack/expo-devtools
items.description: Browser-style devtools that live inside your app: network, console, performance, storage, crashes and a debug tab, behind a draggable button.

items.name: @axonpack/react-pretty-print
items.description: Collapsible JSON and XML trees and a syntax highlighter, from one implementation for React and React Native. You pass the container, text and pressable components in; it owns the logic.

usage.title: One factory, one call
usage.body: No provider to wrap your tree in and no context to thread through it. Configure the client once, call init() at startup, and mount the overlay where you want it.
usage.note: Nothing records anywhere until init() runs — which is what makes shipping the code to production free.

principles.title: How they are built
principles.body: The point of a foundation library is that you stop thinking about it. These are what keep them that way.

items.title: Small and focused
items.body: One package solves one problem. Nothing here grows into a framework that wants to own your app's structure.

items.title: Dependency-light
items.body: Adding a package should not add a supply chain. Where one needs a library you may already have, you hand it over rather than having it installed for you.

items.title: Independently published
items.body: Each package versions and ships on its own, with its own documentation. Installing one never drags in another.

items.title: Honest about limits
items.body: Every guide ends with what the thing cannot do, and why. A number that cannot be measured is not shown rather than invented.

showcase.title: It runs on the device
showcase.body: Not a socket to a desktop window — the panel is part of the app, so it works on a real phone, over a tunnel, and in a release build you deliberately left it in.
